Creating a task for the Meridian benchmark

Your job is the draft. Validation (verifier code, golden runs, pass@8, thresholds) is done by the benchmark owner.

  1. Explore here first. The world is full of intentional imperfections — duplicate rows, ids that resolve nowhere, same-name people, stale documents, near-miss service names. Good tasks are built on them. Try the example queries.
  2. Design a multi-hop question a real employee would ask: the answer should be discrete facts (ids, names, amounts, dates) reachable only by joining 2–4 datasets, with at least one plausible-but-wrong path.
  3. Write the prompt underspecified — no table, file, or tool names. The agent must discover where things live.
  4. Draft atomic rubrics: each one states a single verifiable fact — "The [variable] is [value]" — judged pass/fail only. No "because…". Never join two facts with and/or; express a set as one count rubric plus one rubric per member. Negative rubrics are NOT allowed — never write “does not / never / excludes” claims. Enforce exclusions positively: a count rubric (“The number of X is 3”) plus one membership rubric per member makes any wrong inclusion or omission fail.
  5. Package one folder and zip it: 
    drafts/<your-task-id>/
  DRAFT.md      # sections: Target · Prompt · Expected answer (with an
                # evidence chain: which dataset/query proves each fact)
                # · Proposed rubrics · Traps exploited · Solution-path sketch
  queries.sql   # the exact queries that establish your ground truth
  6. Send the zip to the benchmark owner on Slack. They recompute your answer in code, capture a golden run, calibrate difficulty with pass@8 across four frontier models, and either accept it or return it with hardening notes. Target bar: every model should fail the task at least 2 of 8 runs.

Rules: don't propose editing existing data (specify NEW data if needed — the owner injects it); keep benchmark words like "trap" out of prompts; every fact in your expected answer must be provable by a query you include.
